best.hypothesis: A shared monomial Gram map followed by a cached sparse integer congruence transform can eliminate repeated CAR products across polynomial operators. No performance improvement has been measured.
best.mechanism: Write O_i = sum_a C_ai W_a using distinct nonzero input words. For each monomial Gram coordinate, cache its expansion into operator coordinates. A diagonal monomial coordinate contributes C_ai squared on operator diagonals and 2*C_ai*C_aj off diagonal. An off-diagonal monomial coordinate contributes C_ai*C_bi on diagonals and C_ai*C_bj+C_aj*C_bi off diagonal. Accumulate every canonical row exactly and remove cancellations.
best.assumptions: The supplied monomial_map returns the stated exact integer map with upper-triangular coordinates. Input coefficients are Python integers, and all nonzero words satisfy the specified degree and common-charge constraints. Backend cache storage is passed through payload['cache'].
best.failure_cases: Dense incidence columns can make cached coordinate expansions large. Dictionaries with little word reuse may not amortize constructing the monomial map and its expansions. These affect cost, not exactness; empty operators, arbitrary ordering, large integers, dependencies, and exact cancellations are preserved.

best.hypothesis: A shared Wick-contraction compiler can construct the polynomial Gram map directly, reusing crossings and exterior merges across distinct monomial pairs. This may reduce cold construction cost; no improvement has been measured.
best.mechanism: Normalize and combine each operator's terms, then build sparse coefficient postings. Compile each canonical monomial product by contracting only the left annihilators against the right creators, with cached signed exterior merges for the remaining groups. Homogeneous charge makes every product number conserving, so its canonical adjoint exchanges the creator and annihilator mode tuples with positive sign. Symmetrize each monomial pair, lift it through the postings with the required diagonal factors, and remove exact zeros. The implementation is independent of either monomial-map backend.
best.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the specified degree, integer-coefficient, and homogeneous-charge restrictions. Python integer arithmetic remains exact. All caches are local and initially empty; no external capability is required.
best.failure_cases: Mixed-charge inputs invalidate the unsigned adjoint exchange and are outside the contract. Limited reuse can make cache overhead outweigh savings. Dense postings and large outputs still require substantial coordinate expansion and storage. The implementation has not been executed or benchmarked here.

best.hypothesis: Normalizing and merging shared monomials, compiling their Gram map once, and applying an exact sparse congruence transform can reduce repeated algebra across polynomial operators. No measured improvement is claimed.
best.mechanism: Write each operator as O_i = sum_a C_ai W_a in a shared canonical monomial basis. Transpose the monomial Gram map into lists grouped by basis pair. For each pair, compute its sparse coordinate expansion once and reuse it across all canonical output words. A diagonal basis pair contributes C_ai^2 to coordinate (i,i) and 2*C_ai*C_aj to (i,j). An off-diagonal basis pair contributes C_ai*C_bi to (i,i) and C_ai*C_bj + C_aj*C_bi to (i,j). All normalization, accumulation, and cancellation use exact integers.
best.assumptions: The supplied monomial_map callable returns the stated direct canonical-word-to-coordinate dictionary and stores its persistent cache only in payload['cache']. Input coefficients are Python integers, flags are 0/1, and all nonzero input terms share one charge. CAR normalization preserves that charge and never increases degree.
best.failure_cases: Dense incidence can make the congruence expansion expensive, and transposing the compiled map requires additional memory. Inputs with little shared monomial structure may receive no speed benefit. Worst-case output size remains quadratic in the number of operators. Mixed-charge inputs are outside the backend contract.
